source.title: Gastrointestinal tolerability of once-weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg in adults with overweight or obesity, and the relationship between gastrointestinal adverse events and weight loss
source.source_type: post-hoc pooled analysis of STEP 1-3 randomized phase III trials plus separate STEP 4 randomized-withdrawal analysis
source.primary_source_file: Diabetes Obesity Metabolism - 2021 - Wharton - Gastrointestinal tolerability of once‐weekly semaglutide 2 4 mg in adults.pdf

extraction_metadata.scope_note: Primary article and material supplement were processed as one publication packet. Bibliography entries were not atomized.

atoms.canonical_statement: The analysis evaluated gastrointestinal adverse events with once-weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg in adults with overweight or obesity and examined whether those events contributed to weight loss.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We evaluated gastrointestinal (GI) adverse events (AEs) with once-weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg ... and their contribution to weight loss.

atoms.canonical_statement: STEP 1, STEP 3, and STEP 4 enrolled adults without diabetes who had BMI at least 30 kg/m² or BMI at least 27 kg/m² with at least one weight-related comorbidity.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: STEP 1, 3 and 4 enrolled adults aged ≥18 years with a BMI ≥27 kg/m2 (with ≥1 weight-related comorbidity) or ≥30 kg/m2, without diabetes.

population.label: Adults in STEP 1, STEP 3, and STEP 4 without diabetes

atoms.canonical_statement: STEP 2 enrolled adults with BMI at least 27 kg/m² and type 2 diabetes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Participants in STEP 2 had a BMI of ≥27 kg/m2 plus T2D.

population.label: Adults in STEP 2 with type 2 diabetes and BMI ≥27 kg/m²

atoms.canonical_statement: Semaglutide was initiated at 0.25 mg once weekly and escalated every 4 weeks through 0.5, 1.0, and 1.7 mg to 2.4 mg at week 16.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: initiation at 0.25 mg once weekly for 4 weeks, increased at 4-weekly intervals to 0.5 mg, 1.0 mg, 1.7 mg and finally 2.4 mg at week 16.

exposures.details: Escalated every 4 weeks through 0.5, 1.0, 1.7, then 2.4 mg at week 16

atoms.canonical_statement: Participants unable to tolerate semaglutide 2.4 mg could remain on a lower maintenance dose, with at least one attempt to re-escalate to 2.4 mg.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Participants unable to tolerate 2.4 mg ... were permitted to remain at lower maintenance doses, with at least one attempt to re-escalate to 2.4 mg.

atoms.canonical_statement: Adverse events were elicited with open-ended, non-leading questions, followed at subsequent contacts, and coded using MedDRA version 22.1.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: AE information ... was collected throughout each trial, using open-ended, non-leading verbal questions. ... AEs were coded using ... MedDRA (Version 22.1).

atoms.canonical_statement: The pooled STEP 1-3 gastrointestinal adverse-event analyses were post hoc; on-treatment exposure for adverse events was defined as any trial-product dose within the previous 49 days.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: On-treatment GI AE incidence was evaluated in post-hoc analyses ... participants were considered to be on treatment if any dose of trial product was administered within the previous 49 days.

atoms.canonical_statement: Pooled STEP 1-3 adverse-event percentages and event rates were adjusted using Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel weights, and median event durations were estimated with Kaplan-Meier methods.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: adjusted using Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel weights ... Median durations of GI AEs were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier estimator.

atoms.canonical_statement: The descriptive weight-loss analysis used observed week-68 body-weight data among participants still on treatment, stratified by the presence or absence of gastrointestinal adverse events.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: using observed body weight data from participants who were on treatment and had a body weight assessment at week 68

atoms.canonical_statement: Mediation analysis used a natural-effects model with imputation-based estimation to separate weight-loss effects mediated by gastrointestinal adverse events from effects unrelated to those events.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Mediation analysis used a natural effects model with imputation-based estimation ... separate the overall effects ... into effects mediated by GI AEs ... and those unrelated to GI AEs.

atoms.canonical_statement: STEP 4 evaluated gastrointestinal tolerability after a 20-week open-label semaglutide run-in; only participants tolerating 2.4 mg at week 20 were randomized to continue semaglutide or switch to placebo.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Only those who tolerated the 2.4 mg dose at week 20 were eligible for randomization.

atoms.canonical_statement: Across STEP 1-3, 2117 participants were randomized to semaglutide 2.4 mg and 1262 to placebo.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In total, 2117 participants were randomized to semaglutide 2.4 mg and 1262 to placebo within the STEP 1-3 trials.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that gastrointestinal adverse events were more common with semaglutide 2.4 mg than placebo but were typically mild-to-moderate, non-serious, and transient.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: GI AEs were more common with semaglutide 2.4 mg than placebo, but typically mild-to-moderate and transient.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that semaglutide-induced weight loss was largely independent of gastrointestinal adverse events.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Semaglutide-induced WL was largely independent of GI AEs.

atoms.canonical_statement: The pooled gastrointestinal adverse-event and mediation analyses were post hoc and exploratory.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the pooled analysis and mediation analyses were post hoc and exploratory

atoms.canonical_statement: The mediation analysis did not fully account for the time course of gastrointestinal adverse events.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the time course of GI AEs was not fully accounted for

atoms.canonical_statement: The descriptive weight-loss analysis included only participants who remained on treatment and had a week-68 weight assessment, limiting interpretation for early discontinuers.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: descriptive analyses ... only included participants who remained on treatment and had a body weight assessment at week 68

atoms.canonical_statement: The mediation analysis relied on assumptions about absence of confounding beyond the fitted model for post-randomization gastrointestinal adverse events.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: mediation analysis relies on the assumption that there is no confounding beyond that accounted for in the model

atoms.canonical_statement: In STEP 4, awareness of treatment withdrawal after randomization could have influenced adverse-event reporting.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: awareness of treatment withdrawal could potentially influence AE reporting

atoms.canonical_statement: The controlled clinical-trial environment may not fully reflect gastrointestinal tolerability in routine clinical practice.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the controlled clinical trial environment may differ from routine clinical practice
